# Results — Study 199 (Sales-Growth) on the real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: trailing one-year
revenue growth (SalesGrowth_y = Revenues_y / Revenues_{y-1} - 1) from annual 10-K filings
via the shared EDGAR cache. Returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance).
As-of **2026-06-15**.*

**Definition**:
- SalesGrowth = Revenues_y / Revenues_{y-1} - 1
- Q1 = lowest past sales growth ("value"); Q5 = highest past sales growth ("glamour")
- Hedge = Q1 - Q5 (long value, short glamour) -- positive = LSV hypothesis holds

**Reporting lag**: fundamentals from fiscal year y -> returns in calendar year y+1.
**Universe**: current S&P 500 members with Revenues present (~180+ tickers/year average).
**Window**: 18 years of signal (2008-2025), forecasting returns 2009-2026.

| Sales-growth fingerprint | `9ffae4d859d7` |

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the EDGAR panel covers only current S&P 500 members
projected backwards. Every firm in the panel survived to 2026. All results are upper
bounds on a live strategy -- the true live effect is weaker, possibly nonexistent.

## Quintile returns (sales growth low to high, forward 1 year)

| Quintile | Mean return | Sharpe | HAC t-stat | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Q1 (low growth -- value)** | **+19.7%/yr** | +1.27 | **+8.44** | 89% |
| Q2 | +14.7%/yr | +1.09 | +7.86 | 78% |
| Q3 | +17.3%/yr | +1.41 | +6.76 | 89% |
| Q4 | +16.6%/yr | +1.32 | +8.34 | 89% |
| **Q5 (high growth -- glamour)** | **+20.0%/yr** | +1.28 | **+8.45** | 83% |
| Equal-weight market | +17.7%/yr | +1.38 | +9.24 | 89% |

## Long low-growth / short high-growth hedge (Q1 - Q5, value minus glamour)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Mean annual return | **-0.4%/yr** |
| Sharpe ratio | -0.03 |
| HAC Newey-West t-stat | **-0.17** |
| Hit rate (positive years) | 39% (7/18 years) |
| n (years) | 18 |

> **LSV prediction**: positive hedge (value outperforms glamour). **Actual**: negative
> hedge (-0.4%/yr), wrong direction, and statistically indistinguishable from zero.

## Excess vs equal-weight market

| Arm | Excess return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| Low-growth (Q1) | **+2.0%/yr** | **+1.36** |
| High-growth (Q5) | **+2.4%/yr** | **+1.82** |

Neither excess clears the |t| >= 2 bar. High-growth stocks have a *higher* excess than
low-growth stocks -- opposite of the LSV prediction.

## Random-portfolio null distribution

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|

| Random-control std | 4.9%/yr |
| Low-growth beats random draw | **70%** of 500x18yr draws |

## Verdict

The LSV (1994) glamour/value effect on sales growth is **absent** on this panel.

The hedge of -0.4%/yr (HAC t = -0.17) is statistically indistinguishable from zero and
has the **wrong sign** relative to the LSV prediction (glamour slightly outperforms value).
The low-growth quintile beats only 70% of random same-size draws -- barely above the 50%
chance level.

Importantly, even this null result is an upper bound due to survivorship bias. The panel
excludes firms that were removed from the S&P 500 between 2008-2025, including high-growth
companies that subsequently failed (blowing up in Q5). A live strategy would have been
exposed to those failures, potentially making the hedge even more negative.

The LSV paper's original evidence was strongest in:
- Small-cap and micro-cap stocks (where over-extrapolation is most severe)
- Low-analyst-coverage stocks (where mispricings persist longer)
- The 1968-1990 pre-internet era (where revenue-growth information was less efficiently priced)

None of these conditions apply to the S&P 500 survivor panel in 2008-2025.

- **Signal -- NONE** (HAC t = -0.17 on the hedge; wrong direction; no predictive content
  in revenue-growth rank for future returns on this panel).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE** (no gross edge exists to survive costs; even if the hedge were
  zero, annual rebalancing on large-cap names would leave nothing after any realistic
  transaction cost estimate).
